name: Anatherum

project_scope.selection_mode: Existing three canonical Anatherum species FINISH/ENRICH and genus key only; no first card or native-range reassignment
project_scope.note: Three species are canonical per current manifest, including A. tenuispatheum installed as a provisional card. Original A. glomeratum county PASS and A. virginicum PASS are preserved; A. glomeratum third-county Williamson outside target, needs separate audit. Historical var. pumilus photo now a taxonomic comparison for A. tenuispatheum, not verified glomeratum.

priority: wet-site vs old-field context as secondary support
study_strategy.warning: The familiar Andropogon names are still common in Texas. Search aliases before assuming a record is a separate taxon.

quick_split: Anatherum glomeratum (bushy) — many short densely grouped white-silky paired racemes in a broad crown; source-confirmed Texas macro still required.
Anatherum virginicum (broomsedge) — separated narrow silky flowering groups partly enclosed by conspicuous flattened upper spathes; two licensed original photos now in genus panel.

Anatherum tenuispatheum — distinct accepted taxon, linked to old Andropogon tenuispatheus and old Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus. Current photo is provisional; use a vouchered measured spathe/raceme/spikelet, NOT old broad bushy habit alone.
Andropogon gerardi (big bluestem) — few stout exposed turkey-foot branches; canonical under Andropogon, not a duplicate genus member.
Schizachyrium scoparium (little bluestem) — shorter scattered short silky racemes on upper leafy branches.
Bothriochloa ischaemum (KR) — introduced, several long slender terminal fingers; leaf collar/spikelet confirms.
comparison_lesson.caveat: Current POWO 2026 distinguishes A. tenuispatheum from A. glomeratum, with old var. pumilus under the former. Three species installed in manifest, one provisional taxon photo. No Hays nativity claim recalculated.

look_here_first: THREE INSTALLED ANATHERUM BLUESTEMS: true bushy A. glomeratum forms a broad dense silk-brushed crown; broomsedge A. virginicum has more separated narrow partly spathe-enclosed silky pairs. A. tenuispatheum is a third accepted species; do not identify it from fluffy habit alone and do not misapply old 'Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus' photos to bushy A. glomeratum. At 10–20×, photograph each paired raceme, upper spathe, sessile/pedicellate spikelets, true hairs and measurable awns. Keep uncertain plants Anatherum sp.
shared_genus_traits: Warm-season perennial tufted grasses with leaf sheaths, ligules and narrow blades.
Upper culms bear inflorescence units subtended by spathe-like leafy sheaths.

Each short rame bears paired spikelet positions, typically one fertile sessile spikelet and a reduced or absent pedicellate spikelet; silky hairs on the rame joints and pedicels produce the fluffy appearance.
Andropogon glomeratus and Andropogon virginicus are familiar search aliases for the canonical Anatherum concepts used in this project.

quick_comparison_steps: 1. WHOLE plant: decide broad crowded brush versus separate spathe-held upper flowering units; do not use winter orange color as species proof.
2. CURRENT NAMES: keep A. glomeratum, A. virginicum and A. tenuispatheum distinct; check old Andropogon synonyms, especially var. pumilus.
3. SOURCE PHOTO: use only source-labelled glomeratum museum image for bushy; source-labelled Hawaiian var. pumilus belongs to a DIFFERENT modern taxon concept and remains comparison-only.
4. SCALE: on same vouchered plant photograph intact spathe, two rames, paired sessile/pedicellate spikelet positions, rachis hairs and awn with millimeter scale.
5. If uncertain, Anatherum sp. / bluestem candidate. Do not act on native/introduced management decisions without species determination and separate county-range review.
overlap_and_cautions: Both have silky hairs, paired rames and similar spikelet sizes; those shared traits do not separate the species.
Sheath and rame lengths overlap and can change with maturity; overall inflorescence architecture plus rame exposure is stronger than one measurement.
Bushy bluestem can be less conspicuously fluffy before maturity; broomsedge can look crowded on stressed or mowed plants.
Wet versus dry habitat is supporting context only; broomsedge and bushy bluestem can grow together.
A. virginicum is already canonical with species-level PASS status. The older genus-level HOLD text was stale and is superseded by the species record.

The live Master Plant Pool currently lists the two canonical concepts under familiar Andropogon source names; its Anatherum genus row instead counts Anatherum tenuispatheum. Do not manually overwrite Genus Study Index formula columns C:M to mask this source-name mismatch.

Range data integrity: A. glomeratum species.json lists Hays, Travis and Williamson as three target counties, but Williamson is not in PROJECT_RULES.md target zone. Treat its current PASS as a recorded species status requiring targeted Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review; do not use this genus lesson to independently certify a third target county.

IMPORTANT CURRENT POWO SPLIT (2026): Andropogon glomeratus (unranked binomial) is synonym of Anatherum glomeratum, but Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus is synonym of a SEPARATELY ACCEPTED species, Anatherum tenuispatheum. This makes old Hawaiian var. pumilus photo records unsuitable as A. glomeratum species-example evidence. A. tenuispatheum also differs from A. virginicum (Andropogon virginicus). Never collapse these three canonical installed species or recertify county nativity from image names. Review A. glomeratum existing county PASS separately; its recorded Williamson County is outside project target zone.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.separate: Few open fingerlike turkey-foot racemes, not many paired sheath-enclosed silky rames crowded into a brush.
Silky rames occur singly or in simpler branch arrangements rather than dense upper Anatherum spathe-bracted clusters; confirm spikelet arrangement.
Often conspicuous branching panicles and different raceme/spikelet architecture; inspect rachis and pedicellate spikelets rather than hairiness alone.

visual_comparison.title: ANATHERUM — flowering true bushy bluestem versus broomsedge and tenuispatheum
visual_comparison.subtitle: Six credited panels including new USGS true var. glomeratus flowerhead with two visible head-level arrows, existing regional broomsedge photos and historical var. pumilus correctly labelled different accepted taxon. Need mm-scale spathe/paired-spikelet macro.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: DENSE BRUSH = bushy candidate; SEPARATE SPATHES = broomsedge candidate; VAR. PUMILUS HISTORICAL PHOTO = tenuispatheum name, NOT glomeratum. Actual paired racemes and hairy spikelet anatomy complete the ID.

items.label: TRUE BUSHY BLUESTEM — several dense flowering clusters (USGS Louisiana var. glomeratus)
items.image_role: Actual USGS photograph source-labelled Andropogon glomeratus var. glomeratus; many short crowded silky inflorescence groups and narrow surrounding leaves are visible. Original photograph has no accurate mm scale for rachis/spathe microanatomy.
items.caption: Three narrow, strongly clustered pale-silky flowering plumes rise along a grass culm. The USGS identifies the pictured taxon as Andropogon glomeratus var. glomeratus (modern A. glomeratum, distinct from old var. pumilus). These are genuine visible flowering-cluster features; individual rachilla joints, the precise paired spathes, sessile/pedicellate spikelets, awns and ligule need a dissected millimeter-scale photo. The picture is from Louisiana, NOT proof of occurrence in Hays County.
items.why_it_matters: Adds true var. glomeratus flowering-head architecture for field learning without conflating the Hawaiian var. pumilus/modern A. tenuispatheum records.
items.creator: Larry Allain, U.S. Geological Survey

Original source labelled Andropogon glomeratus var. glomeratus; source is Louisiana, NO Hays provenance.
